content:
maya: quick heads-up — NTK RoPE sweep hit a sharp perf cliff on Mixtral-7B around 8k ctx, need eyes.
alex: wtf — cliff as in latency per token goes up or throughput drops?
jun: saw this in canary too. per-token latency doubles after ~6.5k on some kernels.
maya: exact numbers from profiler (canary build 2026-03-15):
```
model: mixtral-7b ntk-rope variant
sequence: 8192
kernel path: fast_attn_fused (fp16) -> fallback to generic (fp32) at step 6k
avg token ms before cliff: 18.2ms
avg token ms after cliff: 42.7ms
cause: kernel fallback + KV cache spill (memmove thrash)
```
alex: kernel fallback + memmove — sounds like we hit a tiling/stride case that doesn’t fit the fused kernel. did you capture allocs?
maya: yes — allocator logs show transient GPU memory peak and then synchronous copies:
```
[alloc] peak_used 9.1 GB -> requested 11.8 GB -> evict kv-cache partial -> host fallback memcpy -> sync
```
sophie: interestingly, Qwen with same NTK config didn't regress until 16k. suggests model-specific kv layout or head/kv dims matter.
jun: hypothesis: Mixtral's per-head KV dim + RoPE scaling drives stride that breaks our small-block fused kernels. when head_k dim % tile != 0 we hit slow path.
maya: did a small experiment swapping to linear RoPE variant on same weights — cliff moves to ~10k, still worse than qwen.
alex: ok actionable: we should make kernel selection aware of (head_k_dim, kv_stride, avg_seq_len) and prefer the generic kernel preemptively when mem pressure + long ctx predicted. fallback-on-error is too late.
sophie: also think batching heuristics need to consider KV hit ratio. many small requests with prefix-sharing keep KV small but a single long-context user will cause spill. maybe autoscale batch size by max_seq_in_batch rather than avg.
jun: added quick config suggestion for runtime heuristics:
```json
{"kernel_policy": "profiled", "prefallback_threshold_seq": 6000, "kv_memory_margin": 0.15, "batching": {"max_seq_gate": "max_in_batch", "dynamic_batch_cutoff_ms": 30}}
```
maya: ran that locally — preemptive generic kernel reduces peak latency but increases base ms by ~5%. still preferable vs cliff for SLAs.
ci-bot: deploy check: canary tests show 2 regressive cases in perf-suite -> tagging eng-runtime.
alex: next steps: 1) add kernel selection rule using head_k_dim % tile and kv_stride heuristics; 2) update batching gate to use max seq; 3) longer NTK pseudo-runs for Mixtral (0..20k) to map safe ranges; 4) add mem-margin to allocator to avoid memcpy fallback.
sophie: for tracking, observed per-model "safe ranges" in sweep so far (very rough):
- mixtral-7b NTK: safe <= 4096, cliff zone 6k-9k
- mixtral-7b linear: safe <= 8192
- llama-2-13b NTK: safe <= 8192
- qwen-7b YARN: safe up to 32768 (no cliff observed in our runs)
These are preliminary — need more reps.
jun: i can add an automated NTK long-ctx perf job to CI that runs across kernels and records fallback events + mem copies. will instrument kv-stride and head dims in profile.
maya: thanks. also let's gate shipping NTK variant in dedicated pools for Mixtral until we have kernel policy. add a rollout flag.
alex: will draft the kernel heuristic PR and a short perf test plan. include one synthetic workload that forces odd head_k dims to validate path.
sophie: recording threads: #perf-regressions, #runtime-kernels. tagging @alex @jun for follow-ups. :eyes:
maya: good progress. will paste the full profiler dump and sample reproducer in the ticket.
